messages:
Sasha: Heads-up, saw another ingest-proxy OOM during the ecommerce spike. We need to rethink how long we keep unpersisted tokens in memory.
Lee: Can you paste the sketch of options? quick bullets suffice.
Sasha: Short version: keep less in RAM. Options: 1) lease tokens (short-lived) 2) local WAL for queued items 3) force client-side retries + stronger idempotency 4) tiered ack levels.
Priya: I prefer local WAL + ACCEPTED ack. Keeps client behavior unchanged and avoids moving complexity to SDKs. But hosted proxies are ephemeral so WAL = trickier.
Ben: Agree re: WAL tradeoff. For hosted, we need to either replicate the WAL to a durable write path or accept some potential loss windows. Could replicate to the ledger synchronously? defeats latency win.
Sasha: Right. What about hybrid: PROVISIONAL ack for low-cost tenants, ACCEPTED+WAL for mid-tier, PERSISTED for enterprise. Route by tenant config.
Lee: That routing adds a lot of logic but seems practical. We should define the ack enum so downstream systems can reason about event guarantees.
Priya: Suggested enum (proto):

AckLevel.PROVISIONAL // lease: validated, short TTL, not durable
AckLevel.ACCEPTED    // queued locally (WAL optional), reasonably durable, faster than persisted
AckLevel.PERSISTED   // durable on ledger

Sasha: Needs to be surfaceable via SDK and internal traces. Also add origin token metadata: proxy-id + segment-offset + optional client-idempotency-key.
Ben: For dedupe rules, finalizer should prefer events by ack strength: PERSISTED > ACCEPTED > PROVISIONAL. If same idempotency-key seen multiple times, pick first PERSISTED or latest PERSISTED? We need deterministic tie-breaker.
Lee: Determinism matters for billing. Rule: choose the earliest PERSISTED by ingestion-sequence; if none PERSISTED, choose earliest ACCEPTED; if only PROVISIONAL, pick the one with highest proxy priority then earliest timestamp. Document it.
Priya: Edge: client retries after provisional eviction will create new origin-token. If idempotency-key present, finalizer dedupes. If missing, we risk duplicates. We should require idempotency header for any ACCEPTED or PERSISTED attempt; SDKs must set it.
Sasha: We can't break existing clients. Proposal: make idempotency required for upgraded tenants; warn others and default to ACCEPTED with in-memory queue.
Ben: Observability hooks: emit metrics per-ack-level (ingest_ack_level), origin-token, lease-expire-count, eviction-count, wal-replay-duration, time-to-persist. Correlate with billing windows to detect under/over credits.
Lee: Operational pattern: if ingress pressure high, proxies start returning PROVISIONAL and set X-Ingest-Pressure header. SDKs should exponential-backoff or switch to async batching. 429 Retry-After if we drop requests.
Priya: For WAL design notes: ring-buffer files, segment size ~32MB, fsync on segment close or low-latency fsync policy, compact after ledger ack. On restart, replay remaining segments into ledger. Need to watch IO contention.
Sasha: For hosted, instead of relying on local disk we could stream a very cheap replication to a nearby durable ingest service (write-behind) that accepts WAL segments. That service would be multi-tenant and durable; proxies keep tiny RAM buffers and stream to write-behind.
Ben: That feels like adding another service but could be lighter weight than upgrading proxy persistence guarantees. Also allows Dedicated proxies to keep local-only WAL.
Lee: Security: WAL/write-behind must respect tenant encryption keys and not expose other tenants. Encrypt segments at rest and in-flight.
ingest-bot: WARNING: ingest-proxy-9 mem_pressure above threshold: 78% used, provisional mode enabled
Sasha: Ok next steps (short):
- Proto change: AckLevel enum + origin-token fields (Priya)
- WAL spike: implement ring-buffer prototype on single proxy with replay logic (Ben)
- Backpressure header and SDK guidance (Lee)
- Finalizer dedupe doc w/ deterministic tie-breakers + idempotency enforcement plan (Sasha)

Lee: I'll own SDK guidance and add a simple backoff example in JS and Python.
Priya: I'll open RFC draft for dedupe rules and tie-breaker algorithm.
Ben: I'll prototype WAL and run a canary against a low-risk tenant.
Sasha: Thanks team. Follow-up in #eng-platform next week with spikes results. :rocket:
